findings.text: Top level bzip2 decompression driver that accepts either a supplied input image or a fill callback, plus an output destination or flush callback with error reporter and optional consumed-input position. It prepares input and output staging, initializes decoder state, repeatedly pulls decoded bytes and either advances a direct pointer or forwards full chunks to flush, then validates overall integrity before releasing workspace and reporting a status code.
Thin compatibility wrapper around the bzip2 driver that shortens the supplied input length by four before delegating all other arguments unchanged and returning the driver status.

Decoder initializer that allocates and zeroes persistent state, attaches input storage and fill handler with a failing default, builds a big-endian checksum table, validates leading archival framing including a digit-selected block capacity, reserves intermediate decoding storage scaled from that digit, and reports allocation or format failures.

Incremental output producer that copies up to a requested count of decoded bytes into caller storage while maintaining checksum, repeat-count and transform-following cursors across calls, refilling its intermediate store by decoding further input blocks when exhausted and propagating terminal or malformed-input statuses.

Block decode progresses through framing validation, symbol alphabet reconstruction, coding-group selection, per-group table derivation, symbol stream decoding into intermediate storage, transform inversion with occurrence ordering, and output cursor priming, aborting to distinct malformed-input or terminal statuses whenever framing, bounds or table limits are violated.

Output production cycles among emitting pending duplicate bytes, following the reordered sequence to obtain next bytes, interpreting a run-length marker after consecutive duplicates, finalizing a block with checksum folding and mismatch escalation, requesting the next input block, and latching negative terminal counts for all later calls.

Bit extraction maintains a left-shifted reservoir fed one byte at a time to preserve ordering and alignment, refills exhausted input through the fill handler with sticky input-error latching, sheds high reservoir content before overflow, consumes exactly the requested width, and yields zero on input failure.

Framing validation distinguishes data blocks from end-of-stream using paired 24-bit signatures plus a stored 32-bit checksum, rejects a legacy randomized variant, enforces that the initial selector offset lies within intermediate capacity, and requires a leading archival marker whose trailing digit selects capacity within one through nine.

Table construction enforces coding-group count limits, nonzero selector count with recency-based selector decoding guarded by group count, per-symbol length limits, decoded-value bounds against table capacity, intermediate capacity guards for runs and literals, and a sentinel-terminated limit table for symbol resolution.

Integrity handling seeds a per-block checksum to all ones, updates it per emitted byte through a table-driven shift and xor, complements it at block end, folds it into a running total by rotation and xor, forces a file-level mismatch on per-block disagreement, and finally requires stored end-of-stream checksum equality for success.

Literal decoding combines run symbols into repeat counts with doubling weights, resolves other symbols through alphabet translation and recency reordering with frequency accounting, and the output stage treats a byte following three duplicates as a repeat count with distinct countdown seeding for block start versus steady state and with zero meaning exactly three.

Decoder state observed through use includes input staging around inbuf with position and count companions plus a bit reservoir and error latch and a fill callback, intermediate workspace around dbuf with capacity plus selectors and frequency and translation and recency and group tables, output cursors for position and current value and remaining count and pending duplicates and run countdown, and integrity state for per-block and stored and running checksums with a checksum table.

Bit reader failure is signaled with a zero value that is indistinguishable from a legitimate all-zero bit field, so callers cannot detect end of input or refill failure from the return alone and must rely on latched error or downstream validation.

Preboot-style bump allocation aligns every request upward, advances a single global pointer without reclamation, rejects negative sizes, aborts when crossing a global end limit, and counts allocations, so exhaustion, fragmentation from alignment waste and non-thread-safe shared-pointer updates are caller-visible risks.
Gzip input-output staging size is sixteen kibibytes, that is 16384 bytes.

Data blocks are marked by the 24-bit pair 0x314159 and 0x265359 while end of stream uses 0x177245 and 0x385090, each followed by a 32-bit checksum; the stream leader corresponds to characters B Z h with trailing digit one through nine selecting block capacity as that digit times one hundred thousand integers of intermediate storage.

Both default input refill handlers unconditionally report failure with negative one, meaning streams without an explicit fill callback cannot progress past initially supplied bytes and must surface input exhaustion through the error latch.

Top-level driver allocates output staging only when a flush callback is present and input staging only when no input image is supplied, reports staging failures through the error callback, publishes consumed input position when requested, and releases intermediate storage and state and any internally allocated staging in reverse order of acquisition before returning.

Allocation under the name malloc has two build alternates, a bump-pointer routine with alignment and limit checks for constrained early environments and a macro alias to the kernel allocator with its standard flag, so callers see identical naming with different reclamation and failure behavior per build.

Inflate decompression sources select a preboot configuration through dedicated preprocessor markers that gate kernel-header exclusion and early-boot assumptions, indicating these fragments belong to a constrained initialization build rather than normal kernel context.
